scope: Different-author, source-only fail-closed audit of the sealed M1867 additive C2 K8 case0 mapped public-fault X/Z diagnostic package. The audit verifies exact source identity, contract and author double seals, M1863 failed-predecessor authority, docs/359, clean M1867/M1869 namespaces, the one-compile/one-simulation future budget, zero UCLI/SAIF/PTPX, CPython 3.6/3.12 official suites, the exact twelve M1857 and four M1863 synchronized-inventory attacks, and independent predecessor-terminal reachability mutations. No runner, VCS, simv, EDA, license query, attempt, result, release, source/predecessor modification, docs/359 modification, ucli.key access, commit, or push was performed.
verdict: FAIL CLOSED. M1867 fixes both predecessor classes: all exact twelve M1857 mutations and all four M1863 constant-false control-ancestor mutations are rejected on CPython 3.6 and 3.12; the exact SV stop tasks are direct display-then-unconditional-finish sequences. However, the Python checker only rejects direct Return/Raise/Break/Continue statements before publication. Four synchronized mutations insert a nested constant-true return or raise before authority, attempt creation, compile, or the runtime subprocess; all four preserve the counted direct actions and expected ordering but make them unreachable, and all four escape on both runtimes. Therefore execution reachability remains unproved and M1869 must not be created. An additive successor must reject terminal-containing compound predecessors (at minimum constant-true If and unconditional loop/try forms) in main and run, or constrain those statement lists to an explicit allowlist and add these four attacks to both-runtime tests.

findings.title: Nested constant-true terminal predecessors can bypass direct authority, attempt, compile, and subprocess actions
findings.evidence: With each mutated runner SHA synchronized into contract.source_files, both CPython 3.6 and 3.12 accepted: if True:return before verify_authority(); if True:raise before ATTEMPT.mkdir(); if True:return before the unique compile run(); and if True:return inside run() before subprocess.run(). The historical M1857 12/12 and M1863 4/4 attacks were rejected on both runtimes.
findings.impact: A future release could approve a source that returns success without authority or attempt consumption, never compiles, or bypasses the only subprocess. Direct-node cardinality and source order alone do not prove runtime reachability.
findings.required_fix: Create an additive successor. Reject any direct compound predecessor whose body can terminate before each critical action, including constant-true If and equivalent unconditional constructs, in both main and run; alternatively enforce an exact statement-type allowlist for the critical prefixes. Add the four synchronized attacks to official CPython 3.6/3.12 tests, require another different-author source review, and use a fresh release label. Do not create M1869 from M1867.
